introduction: On this Sunday, Moses sets before the people a blessing and a curse, and urges them to keep God's words in their hearts. At the end of the Sermon on the Mount, Jesus says that not everyone who says Lord, Lord, will enter the Kingdom, but those who do the Father's will; the wise build their house on rock. Paul teaches that we are justified freely by God's grace. Let us build our lives on the word of Christ.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, the Lord is our rock and our fortress. Let us bring him our prayers.
intentions: For the Church: that she may not only hear the words of Christ but put them into practice. Let us pray to the Lord.
For families: that they may build their homes on the rock of Christ. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those whose lives have been shaken by storms: that they may find a firm foundation in God. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who think they must earn God's love: that they may discover that we are justified freely by his grace. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that we may do the will of our Father in heaven. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: Lord God, you are our rock and our refuge. Help us to hear the words of your Son and to act on them, so that our lives may stand firm. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: Built on rock
reflection.body:
Moses tells the people to keep God's words close: "you shall lay up these words of mine in your heart and in your soul." He sets a choice before them: "Behold, I set before you today a blessing and a curse." Listening to God's commandments brings blessing; turning away to other gods brings ruin.

Jesus ends the Sermon on the Mount with a similar choice. He warns against a faith of words only: "Not everyone who says to me," Lord, Lord, "will enter into the Kingdom of Heaven, but he who does the will of my Father who is in heaven." Even impressive religious activity is not enough if it is not rooted in a real relationship with him. To some who prophesied and did mighty works in his name, he will say, "I never knew you."

Then Jesus tells a parable about two builders. One builds his house on rock, the other on sand. Both houses face the same storm: "The rain came down, the floods came, and the winds blew." The difference is the foundation. The house on rock stands; the house on sand falls, "and its fall was great." Jesus explains: the wise builder is "Everyone therefore who hears these words of mine and does them."

Storms come to every life. What matters is what we have built on.

Paul reminds us that our foundation is God's gift before it is our work. "for all have sinned, and fall short of the glory of God; being justified freely by his grace." We do not earn God's love. But having received it, we are called to live it out.

This week, choose one teaching of Jesus from the Sermon on the Mount, chapters five to seven of Matthew, and put it into practice. Build on rock, one decision at a time.
